title: Recovery of a Temporary Credit on a Dispute Resolved Against the Cardholder
content:
A temporary credit that still stands on a billing dispute the card records as resolved against the cardholder is owed back to the bank, and this rule fixes how much is rebilled. It governs cards under Personal Credit Cards.

**When it is owed.** The rebill is owed as soon as the dispute stands in that status and is posted at the next reconciliation of the account, whether or not the cardholder is in touch. A card account carrying no dispute recorded as resolved against the cardholder is out of scope of this rule and nothing is rebilled.

**How the rebill is posted.** The rebill is posted by `rebill_card_dispute_credit_f8e84f35`, a tool the agent unlocks and then calls. One call books a single rebill entry on the card's ledger, tied both to the billing dispute it belongs to and to the temporary credit entry it takes back, and dated the day of the call in that day's statement cycle. The same call raises the balance owed on the card account by the rebilled amount, and the cardholder sees the charge on the card's activity list and a larger balance owed.

**Parameters.**

- `card_account_id` — the reference number of the credit card account whose ledger receives the rebill and whose balance owed rises; read from the card account lookup for this cardholder before the call. An identifier.
- `customer_id` — the reference number identifying the cardholder profile the rebilled card account belongs to; read from the customer profile lookup before the call. An identifier.
- `card_dispute_id` — the reference number of the billing dispute this rebill belongs to; read from the card dispute lookup before the call. An identifier.
- `source_item_id` — the reference number of the single temporary credit entry on the card's ledger that is being taken back; read from the card activity lookup before the call. An identifier.
- `rebill_amount` — the money charged back to the cardholder, expressed exactly as the ledger records a money amount: US dollars to 2 decimal places, or an empty string, always a positive number carried to 2 decimal places and rounded half-up. The figure itself is passed, never a proportion or a share.

**Return.** A confirmation sentence in plain text. It names the new ledger entry's own reference number, repeats the rebilled amount in US dollars to two decimals, names the dispute reference number and the card account reference number, and states the balance owed after the rebill, also in US dollars to two decimals. A sentence of that shape means the entry was booked and the balance was raised; anything beginning with Error means nothing was written.
